item.title: Shed destroyed in fire at Delai Saweni car wash
item.description: A SHED at a car wash and tyre centre in Delai Saweni, Lautoka, was completely destroyed by fire on Monday evening. The National Fire Authority (NFA) received a report of the fire from the National Command Centre at about 5.30pm.
item.content:encoded:
A SHED at a car wash and tyre centre in Delai Saweni, Lautoka, was completely destroyed by fire on Monday evening.

The National Fire Authority (NFA) received a report of the fire from the National Command Centre at about 5.30pm.

According to NFA the property owner was reportedly in Sabeto, Nadi, attending a funeral.

“Attempts to contact the business owner were unsuccessful,” the statement from NFA said.

NFA chief executive officer Puamau Sowane said the incident highlighted the importance of fire prevention and early detection.

He urged business and property owners to properly manage electrical systems, appliances, flammable materials and other potential fire hazards.

Mr Sowane also encouraged property owners to install smoke alarms to provide early warning and allow people to evacuate and alert emergency services.

Investigations into the cause of the fire continue.

item.title: FSC marks Pacific milestone with spray drone technology
item.description: THE Fiji Sugar Corporation is set to become the first institution in Fiji and the Pacific to deploy spray drones in sugarcane farming. FSC has procured two DJI spray drones, each with a 20-litre capacity, with support from the Ministry of Agriculture, Waterways and Sugar Industry through its capital grants program.
item.content:encoded:
THE Fiji Sugar Corporation is set to become the first institution in Fiji and the Pacific to deploy spray drones in sugarcane farming.

FSC has procured two DJI spray drones, each with a 20-litre capacity, with support from the Ministry of Agriculture, Waterways and Sugar Industry through its capital grants program.

The move marks a major step in FSC’s efforts to mechanise and modernise the sugar industry while improving farming efficiency and productivity.

Ten FSC officers have begun a 10-day specialised training program at the FSC Training Centre to operate the drones.

The program is being delivered by Aerolab and Drone Trust Consultancy of New Zealand in accordance with Civil Aviation Authority of Fiji (CAAF) guidelines.

Upon completing the training and receiving CAAF certification, the officers will be eligible to operate the drones for commercial spraying applications.

FSC said it would be the first institution in Fiji and the Pacific to train and certify officers specifically to operate spray drones and put the technology into use for sugarcane growers.

The training program was launched in the presence of Ministry of Agriculture, Waterways and Sugar Industry director Praneel Naidu and members of FSC’s executive management team.

Mr Naidu highlighted the role of drone technology in advancing agricultural mechanisation and its potential for wider applications across the farming sector.

FSC said the technology could improve crop management, farming efficiency and productivity while contributing to better cane quality and sugar recovery.

The initiative is also expected to provide sugarcane growers with access to modern spraying technology that can make crop management safer and more efficient.

FSC acknowledged the Ministry’s support through its capital grants program, which enabled the purchase of the two drones.

item.title: Lalabalavu: Constitution belongs to the people
item.description: FIJI’S constitutional future must not be dictated by politicians, political parties or institutions, President Ratu Naiqama Lalabalavu says, stressing that ordinary citizens must remain at the heart of any constitutional reform process. Ratu Naiqama said the Constitution was too important to be controlled by any single institution.
item.content:encoded:
FIJI’S constitutional future must not be dictated by politicians, political parties or institutions, President Ratu Naiqama Lalabalavu says, stressing that ordinary citizens must remain at the heart of any constitutional reform process.

Ratu Naiqama said the Constitution was too important to be controlled by any single institution.

“Not a single individual or no single institution should own Fiji’s constitutional future,” he said.

“A constitution is too important for that.”

He said the Constitution belonged to the people and citizens must have a meaningful opportunity to determine its future.

“The constitution therefore belongs not merely to lawyers, judges, politicians, or public officials. It belongs to the people.”

He said the presentation of the report should not bring the public conversation to an end.

“Our people must remain participants in constitutional reform, not become observers of decisions made on their behalf.”

Ratu Naiqama called for transparency and civic education if constitutional amendments were proposed, saying people must understand what was changing, why it was being changed and what the consequences could be.

“It will require time for citizens to think, ask questions, and make informed decisions.”

He said the credibility of any final outcome would depend not only on the amendments themselves but on the integrity of the process used to develop them.

item.title: Approach findings calmly, says PM
item.description: THE recommendations in the Constitutional Review Commission’s report reflect views put forward by Fijians who made the effort to participate in the review process, Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka said while urging the public to approach the findings calmly and respectfully as Cabinet considers the way forward. “It’s not the government yet,” Mr Rabuka said.
item.content:encoded:
THE recommendations in the Constitutional Review Commission’s report reflect views put forward by Fijians who made the effort to participate in the review process, Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka said while urging the public to approach the findings calmly and respectfully as Cabinet considers the way forward.

“It’s not the government yet,” Mr Rabuka said.

“It’s the views of the people who made the effort to submit their views.”

He stressed that the recommendations should not be interpreted as Government policy or decisions.

“These are recommendations, not decisions of Government.

“Cabinet will now carefully consider what has been proposed before determining the way forward.”

The Prime Minister’s comments come as public debate intensifies over the report, particularly its recommendation on Fiji’s status as a secular state.

Mr Rabuka acknowledged the concern but said his Christian faith should not be interpreted as support for a division of Fijians along religious lines.

“My Christian faith is well known. But I have said previously that simply declaring Fiji a Christian state is not what makes us Christian.

“Christianity should be reflected in the way we live — through humility, kindness, compassion, hard work, service and love for one another.”

He said people of all faiths had an important place in Fiji and should feel secure in practising their religion.

Mr Rabuka also urged political leaders to be measured in their response and warned against misinformation and inflammatory commentary online.

item.title: FBC to pay damages
item.description: THE Supreme Court has ordered the Fiji Broadcasting Corporation to pay $150,000 in general damages to medical practitioner Dr Shanjivan Padarath for online defamation. The ruling, delivered on August 28 by Justices Anthony Gates, Terence Arnold, and Lowell Goddard, quashed a Court of Appeal decision and reinstated a High Court decision which had found liability against FBC and reporter Savaira Tab
item.content:encoded:
THE Supreme Court has ordered the Fiji Broadcasting Corporation to pay $150,000 in general damages to medical practitioner Dr Shanjivan Padarath for online defamation.

The ruling, delivered on August 28 by Justices Anthony Gates, Terence Arnold, and Lowell Goddard, quashed a Court of Appeal decision and reinstated a High Court decision which had found liability against FBC and reporter Savaira Tabua.

The case related to an online news article published by FBC in September 2016 titled “Fake Doctor to appear in Court” alongside a photograph of Dr Padarath. The image had been pulled from FBC’s archive footage of an earlier, legitimate public health broadcast on conjunctivitis in which Dr Padarath was featured.

Although the text referred to an unnamed and unqualified individual operating a home clinic in Nasinu, readers and colleagues recognised Dr Padarath from the accompanying photograph and named and defended him in their comments on the article.

Justice Goddard highlighted that an article, headline, and illustrative photograph must be evaluated as a whole. The court found that using Dr Padarath’s image created a natural implication that he was the fake doctor, making the publication inherently defamatory.

In addition to the $150,000 damages award, FBC is to pay six per cent interest backdated to March 2023, along with $19,000 in legal costs.

item.title: Turning challenges into triumphs
item.description: FOR Devendra Singh of Qereqere, Bua, yaqona is the foundation of his livelihood and the measure of his resilience. Managing over 3,000 plants across 45 acres, Singh has built his farm through persistence and careful planning, harvesting three times a year with around 500 plants each cycle.
item.content:encoded:
FOR Devendra Singh of Qereqere, Bua, yaqona is the foundation of his livelihood and the measure of his resilience.

Managing over 3,000 plants across 45 acres, Singh has built his farm through persistence and careful planning, harvesting three times a year with around 500 plants each cycle.

The rewards of his hard work are visible in the investments he has made – machinery, vehicles, yaqona pounding machine, a solar dryer and the construction of firewood fuelled yaqona drier for rainy season that strengthen his farming operations and reflect the stability he has achieved.

Behind the numbers, however, is a story of struggle and determination.

Singh has faced the frustration of thieves who not only steal but also harvest prematurely, undermining months of effort.

He has also battled kava dieback, a disease that has crippled many farmers in the North.

Instead of giving in, Singh chose to fight back, he hired contract workers to secure his harvests and introduced a greenhouse system to raise seedlings.

This innovation gave him control over plant health and reduced the impact of dieback, ensuring that his farm could continue to thrive.

His yaqona reaches roadside stalls and the Labasa market, where it sells between $130 and $170 per kilogram across three grades and buyers know his produce for its consistency and quality.

Singh has also diversified into turmeric, showing foresight in making sure his land continues to generate value beyond yaqona.

What makes Singh’s story worthy is not just the scale of his farm but the way he has responded to challenges.

He has turned setbacks into opportunities, investing in solutions that protect his crops and secure his future.

His success supports local employment, assistance in times of need for communities around him and strengthens the supply of yaqona to Labasa.

Singh’s journey offers a lesson for other farmers that challenges will always come but success lies in how you respond, protect your crops, invest in solutions that strengthen your farm and diversify to secure your future.

item.title: Chaudhry calls for release of report
item.description: SECRECY over Fiji’s Constitution Review Commission report is fuelling public anxiety and tensions, says Fiji Labour Party leader Mahendra Chaudhry as he calls for the immediate release of the full report and draft. Mr Chaudhry said provisions from the draft circulating in the media raised serious questions about equal citizenship, including how the President would be chosen, the role of the Great
item.content:encoded:
SECRECY over Fiji’s Constitution Review Commission report is fuelling public anxiety and tensions, says Fiji Labour Party leader Mahendra Chaudhry as he calls for the immediate release of the full report and draft.

Mr Chaudhry said provisions from the draft circulating in the media raised serious questions about equal citizenship, including how the President would be chosen, the role of the Great Council of Chiefs and whether Fiji’s secular character would be weakened.

He rejected Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka’s call for the public to remain calm while Cabinet considers the recommendations.

“That is not an answer to the people’s anxiety,” he said.

He said the failure to publish the full report was creating unnecessary tension and apprehension, particularly in Fiji’s plural society.

“A constitution belongs to the people. It must be debated in the open, or it has no legitimacy.”

Mr Chaudhry also criticised the media exclusion at the commission’s presentation to the President, saying it undermined the Government’s promise of openness and media freedom.

He said the 2013 Constitution was not beyond criticism but provided a clear framework for equal citizenship and rights protecting all communities.

Mr Chaudhry warned that any proposed change that weakened those protections or placed the country’s highest office in the hands of a small appointed committee would face serious public scrutiny.

“A constitution written for the people cannot be delivered in secret.”

He called for the complete report and draft to be released so Fijians could examine and debate the proposed changes openly.

item.title: Taxi operators oppose move
item.description: LAUTOKA taxi operators are urging regulators to freeze current fares, warning that planned reductions will trigger unsustainable recalibration costs alongside rising maintenance expenses. The Fijian Competition and Consumer Commission (FCCC) announced that interim fare adjustments introduced on July 1, 2026, to absorb surging global fuel prices, would expire on September 30. From October 1, fares
item.content:encoded:
LAUTOKA taxi operators are urging regulators to freeze current fares, warning that planned reductions will trigger unsustainable recalibration costs alongside rising maintenance expenses.

The Fijian Competition and Consumer Commission (FCCC) announced that interim fare adjustments introduced on July 1, 2026, to absorb surging global fuel prices, would expire on September 30. From October 1, fares will revert to previous rates, forcing every taxi meter nationwide to be reprogrammed.

Duiyasana Taxis and Tours Cooperative Ltd chairman Rupeni Tabutabu pleaded with authorities to maintain the current rate of $2.14 per 100 metres rather than reverting to $2.10.

“We are pleading with the Government and FCCC if the fare can remain at $2.14 per 100 metres,” he said.

“Don’t just look at the fuel because definitely every month fuel prices fluctuate.”

Mr Tabutabu highlighted that technicians charge up to $50 per meter calibration, creating a heavy recurring burden for operators who paid for reprogramming just weeks ago.

“So when we calibrate the meter, Safeway Electronics is charging $55, another company is charging $50.

“But we will survive if the fare remains at $2.14.”

FCCC’s chief executive officer Jiuta Senikavika defended the temporary measure, saying the regulator must balance consumer protection with industry viability while monitoring global economic shifts.
